scenes.say: Inside almost every cell you have, there's two meters of thread.
It's DNA. Stretched end to end, about two meters of it, in a single cell.
And it's packed into a nucleus about ten micrometers wide.
So how much longer is the thread than the box it lives in?
About two hundred thousand times longer.
If the nucleus were a basketball, the DNA inside would be forty eight kilometers long.
And what's written on all that thread?
About three billion letters from each parent. Six billion in every cell, paired up like the rungs of a ladder.
All of it folded, right now.
